name: Media, Fictionality, and Real World Impact
description: In this special course students will learn rhetorical fictionality theory, and gain an overview of its development and antecedents in narratology. They will analyze fictionality inside and outside fiction as well as across media and genres, and how its diversity complicates core concepts in fiction, such as author and narrator. The course will help understand how fiction and fictionality is put to use in novels, short stories, tv-series, advertisements, campaigns and movies to influence beliefs about the real world impact, with illustrative and practical based focus on how fictionality contribute to circulation of norms of gender and sexuality.
